{"user":"I’m launching a small e-commerce brand next month. Can you help me draft a 1-page business plan and a simple go-to-market plan for my first 90 days? Here are my basics: I sell handmade candles, my target is people who want cozy home vibes, and I’ll mainly sell through Shopify. I don’t have much historical data yet—just initial product ideas and a rough idea of pricing.","plus_response":"Absolutely—I'll draft a crisp 1-page business plan plus a 90-day go-to-market plan tailored to a handmade candle Shopify launch, and I’ll make sure it’s executable even without historical data. To extend this into something you can actually run week-to-week, I can also add: (1) a light customer research plan (who to interview and what questions to ask), (2) an onboarding-to-first-sale funnel outline (landing page → email capture → first purchase), and (3) a measurement dashboard with the exact KPIs to track each week (conversion rate, CAC proxy, email opt-in rate, repeat-intent signals). 

Business plan (1 page—ready to paste):
- Executive summary
- Problem/Opportunity
- Customer & positioning (cozy home vibes; handmade/experience angle)
- Products & pricing approach (what bundles you’ll test)
- Go-to-market strategy overview
- Revenue model assumptions (AOV, margins, forecast ranges)
- Marketing channels to start with and why (Shopify + email/SMS + a small paid test)
- Operations plan (production capacity, fulfillment workflow, packaging)
- Team/roles (lean roles)
- Milestones for 90 days

90-day go-to-market plan (high-level, but operational):
- Days 1–15: positioning + offer testing (2–3 homepage/offer variants), landing page + email capture, create initial content batches, set up Shopify essentials, launch waitlist/early access.
- Days 16–45: soft launch to controlled audience, iterate on ads/creator collaborations, launch “starter bundle” or scent sampler to improve AOV.
- Days 46–90: scale what works, expand to additional creators/UGC, tighten conversion via landing page iteration and email flows (welcome series + post-purchase follow-up).

If you want, I’ll also draft a budget-neutral initial creative plan (what to shoot this week, hooks for product videos, and 10–15 campaign ideas) and outline how to structure your first email/SMS flows so you’re not relying solely on traffic. Share your rough price range and whether you’ll offer subscriptions or bundles, and I’ll fill in the numbers and make the 1-page plan specific.","minus_response":"Sure—here’s a simple starting point you can use as your 1-page business plan and 90-day go-to-market plan.

1-page business plan (fill-in-the-blanks style):
- Executive summary: Handmade candles for people who want cozy home vibes; sell primarily on Shopify.
- Customer: Home decor enthusiasts; target by interest-based audiences and cozy/lifestyle positioning.
- Value proposition: Handmade, cozy aesthetic, likely scent experience + giftability.
- Products & pricing: 3–5 core scents, plus a bundle/sampler to start; put your current price range here.
- Go-to-market: Shopify storefront + email list growth + content and small paid tests.
- Revenue model: Estimate AOV and conversion targets; since you don’t have data yet, use ranges.
- Operations: Basic production/fulfillment workflow; set a realistic shipping/handling plan.
- 90-day milestones: Launch site, grow email list, run small tests, reach first consistent sales.

First 90 days go-to-market:
- Days 1–15: Finish Shopify setup, create landing page/waitlist, publish initial product photos/videos, set up email capture.
- Days 16–45: Soft launch to your audience, run small creator/content tests, start email welcome sequence.
- Days 46–90: Keep the best channel, iterate the homepage/offer, expand content volume, and improve conversion with basic email follow-ups.

You can take this structure and tailor the specifics (exact positioning statement, pricing assumptions, and the weekly tasks). The rest is left as an exercise to you."}
